title: Time, from my Raspberry Pi.
intro: I built a Stratum 1 time server at home. These clocks use its GPS/PPS time when connected, displayed in your timezone, mine, and UTC.
deviceOffset: Estimated correction to your device clock
refreshValue: Every 60 seconds while this tab is visible
offsetNote: A positive correction means the Pi clock was ahead of your device at synchronization. This is an estimate, limited by network delay.
sourceBody: My Raspberry Pi gets time from a GPS receiver and its pulse-per-second signal. It also serves NTP to my home network. This page reads that same disciplined system clock through a small time API.

steps.title: GPS → Raspberry Pi
steps.body: GPS and PPS discipline the Pi clock. The API checks that PPS is selected, Stratum 1 is reported, and synchronization is healthy.

steps.title: Pi → Cloudflare
steps.body: A protected tunnel carries fresh timestamps to the website. The browser never receives the service credentials.

steps.title: Cloudflare → Your browser
steps.body: Three samples estimate the time correction. The browser advances that clock locally between synchronizations.

accuracyBody: The digits show milliseconds, but they do not promise millisecond accuracy. I subtract the Pi's processing time from the round trip and estimate the return journey as half the remaining delay. Unequal travel times still introduce error.
fallbackBody: If the request fails, times out, or reports an unhealthy clock, every display immediately uses Your Device Clock (Fallback). Your timezone comes from your browser settings; it does not decide the synchronized time.
meterNote: Device minus GPS time. Shaded band: ± half the network round trip, an estimate rather than guaranteed accuracy.
